title: Roles and priority decide who changes what; others send change requests
rationale: Decided 2026-10-10. Owner changes anything, including roles and priorities; Engineer changes part details and CAD items; Purchaser changes supplier data and orders; Viewer changes nothing. When two members edit one field, the higher priority wins; on a tie, the app asks. Others send a change request that a higher-priority member accepts or rejects. Replaces users.can_edit_catalog.

title: A team code on the team server names the team's KiCad libraries
rationale: User decision 2026-10-17 (kicad-parts-f397, ADR 0015). One person works for several teams, so libraries are named CODE-Parts and CODE-Resistor_SMD. Boards save footprint library names, so the code belongs to the team: team_settings holds it, and POST /api/team/code sets it once. Folders are kicad-libraries/CODE, tied to the settings record ID.

name: HTTPS to team servers: one ServerTrust for REST and realtime
description: Seed kicad-parts-5ac5. tls.rs builds one rustls config (ring, rustls-platform-verifier) and implements ureq 2's TlsConnector, so ureq needs no tls feature. Realtime wraps its own socket in the same setup. ConnectionProblem in connection.rs maps every failure to one plain message. Tests trust an rcgen authority through the test-trust feature, never the OS store (ADR 0017).
Walking an error chain with source() never found the rustls error inside an io::Error. io::Error::source returns the wrapped error's own source, not the wrapped error.
resolution: Look inside with io::Error::get_ref and downcast_ref, as problem_in_io in crates/collaboration/src/connection.rs does.
